answer: CD14 Mono (classical CD14+ monocytes) has the highest number of significantly differentially expressed genes after AAV9 mini-dystrophin treatment: 315 of the 316 genes tabulated for that cell type pass p_val_adj < 0.05 (152 up, 163 down), well ahead of the runner-up CD16 Mono (240) and NK cells (118). The result is unchanged under the |avg_log2FC| > 0.25 sensitivity check (identical counts for every cell type). Key caveats: (1) counts are taken from the pre-computed supplemental DEG tables, whose per-sheet gene lists appear differently pre-filtered (row counts range from 11 to 3,142, with four cell types — Eryth, pDC, Plasmablast, Platelet — having zero significant genes and sheets like CD4 Naive 30/30 and CD14 Mono 315/316 nearly fully significant), so the ranking partly reflects what was tabulated per cell type; (2) the h5ad↔xlsx linkage is unverified — the h5ad is a CoNGA TCR+GEX object for 5 donors with Pre/Post samples whose obs columns (Status, donor, origin, clusters_gex, etc.) contain no named cell-type labels, so the DEG tables could not be recomputed or cross-checked from the h5ad, and per-cell-type cell counts could not be derived from it.
